description: Iconic fenestrated tropical vine with large glossy leaves. Climbs with aerial roots; give a moss pole.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid, half-strength, every 4-6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
rotation: Quarter turn every 2-3 weeks for even growth.
grooming_propagation: Wipe broad leaves monthly. Propagate by stem cuttings with a node in water or sphagnum moss.
symptoms: Yellowing = overwater; brown crisp edges = low humidity or tap-water salts; drooping = thirst.
toxicity_notes: Calcium oxalate crystals: irritating to pets and kids if chewed; keep out of reach.

description: Trailing vine with heart-shaped leaves, very forgiving for beginners. Tolerates low light.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 6-8 weeks in growing season; pause in winter.
rotation: Turn occasionally so vines grow evenly.
grooming_propagation: Trim leggy vines. Roots easily in water from node cuttings.
symptoms: Yellow leaves = overwater; brown spots = underwater or sunburn.
toxicity_notes: Calcium oxalate: toxic to cats/dogs if ingested; mild skin irritant.

description: Upright sword-like leaves, nearly indestructible. Excellent low-light beginner plant.
fertilizing: Cactus fertilizer once or twice in spring/summer only.
grooming_propagation: Cut off damaged leaves at base. Propagate by leaf cuttings or division.
symptoms: Mushy brown base = root rot from overwater; wrinkled leaves = severely underwater.
toxicity_notes: Saponins: mildly toxic to pets and kids; causes nausea if ingested.

description: Waxy, dark green upright foliage on thick stems. Very low light and drought tolerant.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid half-strength every 2-3 months in growing season; pause in winter.
rotation: Turn every few months for symmetrical growth.
grooming_propagation: Wipe leaves occasionally. Propagate by leaf cuttings or division of rhizomes.
symptoms: Yellow mushy stems = overwater/root rot; wrinkled stems = underwater.
toxicity_notes: Calcium oxalate: toxic to cats/dogs; skin irritant. Wash hands after handling.

description: Glossy leaves with white spade-shaped blooms. Dramatically wilts when thirsty, perks up after water.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Remove spent flower stalks at base. Propagate by division.
symptoms: Dramatic droop = needs water; brown tips = low humidity or fluoride/tap salts; yellow = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Calcium oxalate: toxic to cats/dogs and irritating to kids; keep out of reach.

description: Arching grassy leaves with baby plantlets on long stems. Non-toxic and air-purifying.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Clip off spiderettes and root in water or soil. Trim brown tips.
symptoms: Brown tips = fluoride/chlorine in tap water or low humidity; pale leaves = too much light.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Large round leaves with silvery-green stripes. Folds leaves up at night. Demanding but rewarding.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid half-strength monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Remove brown/yellow leaves at base. Propagate by division in spring.
common_pests: Spider mites, aphids, mealybugs, fungus gnats.
symptoms: Brown crisp edges = hard tap water or low humidity; curling = underwater or cold draft.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Large violin-shaped leaves on a single stem. Popular statement plant but sensitive to changes.
fertilizing: Fiddle-leaf or balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
rotation: Quarter turn weekly; phototropic, leans toward light.
grooming_propagation: Dust leaves with damp cloth. Propagate by stem cuttings or air layering.
symptoms: Leaf drop = shock, overwater, or draft; brown spots = root rot or sunburn.
toxicity_notes: Sap irritates skin and stomach; mildly toxic to pets and kids.

description: Thick, waxy, dark green leaves. Grows into a small indoor tree with proper light.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
rotation: Turn monthly for upright, symmetrical growth.
grooming_propagation: Wipe leaves to keep glossy. Propagate by stem cuttings or air layering.
symptoms: Yellow lower leaves = overwater or low light; leaf drop = cold draft or shock.
toxicity_notes: Latex sap is irritating; toxic to cats/dogs if ingested.

description: Trailing vine with glossy heart-shaped leaves. Very easy and fast-growing.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim vines to encourage bushiness. Roots readily in water from node cuttings.
symptoms: Yellow leaves = overwater; leggy growth = too little light; brown = underwater.
toxicity_notes: Calcium oxalate: toxic to cats/dogs; irritating to kids.

description: Lush, arching fronds. Classic porch and hanging-basket fern; needs steady moisture and humidity.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid half-strength every 4-6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim dead fronds at base. Propagate by division.
symptoms: Crisp brown fronds = low humidity or underwater; yellowing = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Succulent with thick fleshy leaves containing soothing gel. Loves bright sun and neglect.
fertilizing: Succulent fertilizer once in spring; none in winter.
grooming_propagation: Harvest outer leaves for gel. Propagate by offsets (pups).
symptoms: Soft mushy leaves = overwater/rot; thin curled leaves = underwater.
toxicity_notes: Gel is safe topically; the latex layer is toxic to pets if ingested.

description: Rosette-forming succulent with plump pastel leaves. Needs bright light to stay compact.
fertilizing: Succulent fertilizer once in spring; none in winter.
rotation: Turn weekly to prevent stretching toward light.
grooming_propagation: Remove dead lower leaves. Propagate by leaf or stem cuttings.
symptoms: Stretching/leggy = not enough light; mushy translucent leaves = overwater/rot.
toxicity_notes: Generally safe for pets and kids.

description: Compact plant with fuzzy leaves and purple/pink/white flowers. Prefers steady warmth.
fertilizing: African violet fertilizer every 2-4 weeks while blooming; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Remove spent blooms and dusty leaves gently. Propagate by leaf cuttings.
symptoms: Crown rot = water in center/overwater; no bloom = too little light or fertilizer.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Long arching sprays of flat, moth-like flowers. Epiphyte; roots need air and bark medium.
fertilizing: Orchid fertilizer weakly weekly in spring/summer; reduce in winter.
grooming_propagation: Cut spent spike above a node to rebloom. Propagate by keikis or division.
symptoms: Silvery-grey roots = time to soak; yellow leaves = overwater or too much sun.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Epiphytic plant with no soil needs; absorbs water through leaves. Great for terrariums and mounts.
fertilizing: Air-plant fertilizer diluted in soak water once a month in spring/summer.
grooming_propagation: Soak 20-30 min weekly, shake out, dry upside-down within 4 hours. Propagate by pups.
symptoms: Curling/rolling leaves = underwater; brown mush at base = rot from not drying.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Trailing succulent vine with waxy leaves and fragrant star-shaped flower clusters.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Don't remove spent flower spurs - new blooms form there. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Wrinkled leaves = underwater; yellow = overwater; no flowers = too little light.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Trailing succulent with bead-like leaves. Perfect for hanging baskets.
fertilizing: Succulent fertilizer once in spring; none in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim trailing stems. Propagate by stem cuttings laid on soil.
symptoms: Shrivelled beads = underwater; mushy beads = overwater/rot.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats/dogs if ingested; keep hanging out of reach.

description: Round coin-like leaves on thin stems. Produces baby pups at the base.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Separate pot pups and pot them up. Remove damaged leaves.
symptoms: Curling leaves = underwater or too much light; yellowing = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Spiky leaves on slender cane stems. Upright, architectural floor plant.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim canes to encourage branching. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Brown leaf tips = fluoride in tap water or low humidity; yellow = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

description: Feathery, arching palm fronds. Adds humidity and a tropical feel.
fertilizing: Palm fertilizer every 6-8 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim brown fronds at base. Propagate by division.
symptoms: Brown tips = low humidity or tap salts; yellow fronds = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Compact palm with delicate arching fronds. Tolerates lower light than most palms.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 8-10 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim brown fronds at base. Slow grower; repot rarely.
symptoms: Brown tips = underwater or low humidity; yellow = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Graceful tree with drooping branches and small glossy leaves. Sensitive to moving.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
rotation: Avoid moving; drops leaves when relocated.
grooming_propagation: Prune to shape. Propagate by stem cuttings or air layering.
symptoms: Leaf drop = shock, draft, or overwater; sticky leaves = scale/mealybugs.
toxicity_notes: Sap irritates skin; mildly toxic to pets and kids.

description: Tree-like succulent with thick oval leaves. Long-lived; symbol of good luck.
fertilizing: Succulent fertilizer once in spring; none in winter.
grooming_propagation: Prune to shape. Propagate easily from leaf or stem cuttings.
symptoms: Wrinkled leaves = underwater; soft mushy leaves = overwater/rot.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

description: Flat segmented stems with bright pink/red flowers around winter holidays.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly spring through early fall; reduce after blooming.
grooming_propagation: Twist off stem segments and root in soil. Needs short days to rebloom.
symptoms: Bud drop = draft or overwater; limp segments = underwater or root rot.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Waxy heart-shaped flowers (spathes) in red, pink, or white with glossy leaves.
fertilizing: High-phosphorus liquid every 6-8 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Remove spent blooms at base. Propagate by division.
symptoms: Yellow = overwater; brown tips = low humidity or cold draft.
toxicity_notes: Calcium oxalate: toxic to cats/dogs; irritating sap.

description: Patterned leaves in silver, green, and red. Very tolerant of low light.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 6-8 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim yellow leaves at base. Propagate by stem cuttings or division.
symptoms: Yellow = overwater; brown tips = low humidity or tap salts.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

description: Large broad leaves with creamy variegation. Can grow tall indoors.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Wipe leaves. Propagate by stem cuttings; wear gloves (sap irritates).
symptoms: Yellow = overwater; brown tips = low humidity; drooping = underwater.
toxicity_notes: Calcium oxalate causes temporary speech loss ('dumb cane') and irritation; toxic to pets and kids.

description: Bright green, spoon-shaped fronds radiating from a central nest. Loves humidity.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid half-strength every 6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Remove old outer fronds at base. Propagate by spores (difficult) or division.
symptoms: Brown crisp fronds = low humidity or underwater; yellow center = overwater/rot.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Oval leaves with red veins; folds upward at night like praying hands.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid half-strength every 4-6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim brown tips. Propagate by division or stem cuttings.
symptoms: Leaves not closing = too much light; brown edges = hard water or low humidity.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Compact plant with thick, glossy, spoon-shaped leaves. Great for desks.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim leggy stems. Propagate by leaf or stem cuttings.
symptoms: Dropping leaves = overwater; wrinkled = underwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Showy, patterned foliage and colorful blooms. Prefers humidity and gentle light.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 2-4 weeks while growing/blooming; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Remove spent blooms. Propagate by leaf or stem cuttings.
symptoms: Brown leaf edges = low humidity or underwater; yellow = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs (especially tubers); irritating to kids.

description: Large, dramatic arrowhead leaves with striking veins. Dormant in winter.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 2-4 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter dormancy.
grooming_propagation: Trim old leaves at base. Propagate by corm division or offsets.
symptoms: Yellow = overwater; drooping = underwater or cold; brown edges = low humidity.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs; irritating sap.

description: Smaller, perforated leaves than M. deliciosa; trailing or climbing habit.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 4-6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim vines. Propagate by node cuttings in water or moss.
symptoms: Yellow = overwater; brown crisp edges = low humidity.
toxicity_notes: Calcium oxalate: toxic to cats/dogs if ingested.

description: Small fenestrated leaves resembling a miniature Monstera deliciosa.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim to encourage climbing. Propagate by stem cuttings with node.
symptoms: Yellow = overwater; no splits = too little light.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

description: Arrow-shaped leaves that change form as the plant matures; trailing or climbing.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim to keep bushy or let climb. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Yellow = overwater; brown = underwater or low humidity.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs; irritating sap.

description: Small trailing plant with vividly veined leaves in pink, red, or white.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid half-strength every 4 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Pinch to encourage bushiness. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Dramatic wilt = underwater (recovers after water); yellow = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Silvery markings on green, textured leaves. Upright and compact.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Pinch back to keep compact. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Leaf drop = overwater or cold; leggy = too little light.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Boldly colored leaves in red, orange, yellow, and green. Needs bright light for color.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 4-6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Prune to shape. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Leaf drop = shock or draft; faded color = too little light.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs; sap irritates skin.

description: Broad arching leaves on thick woody canes. Tolerates low light and neglect.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 6-8 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim cane to encourage branching. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Brown tips = fluoride in tap water; yellow = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

description: Tree-like with stiff, sword-like leaves on a thick trunk. Drought tolerant.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid every 2-3 months in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim trunk to encourage branching. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Yellowing = overwater; drooping = underwater.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

description: Bulbous trunk stores water; long thin leaves arch like a ponytail. Very drought tolerant.
fertilizing: Succulent fertilizer once or twice in spring/summer; none in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim brown leaf tips. Propagate by seed or offsets.
symptoms: Soft trunk = overwater/rot; brown crisp leaves = underwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Compact form of fiddle leaf fig with smaller leaves; better for small spaces.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Dust leaves. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Leaf drop = shock or overwater; brown spots = sunburn or rot.
toxicity_notes: Sap irritates; mildly toxic to pets and kids.

description: Stiff, feather-like fronds on a short trunk. Very slow-growing, long-lived.
fertilizing: Cycas/palm fertilizer twice in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Remove old fronds at base. Propagate by seed or offsets (pups).
symptoms: Yellow fronds = overwater or nutrient lack; brown = sunburn or cold.
toxicity_notes: Extremely toxic to pets and kids (all parts, especially seeds); can be fatal if ingested.

description: Showy, fragrant trumpet flowers. Often sold as potted gift plants.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid while growing and blooming; stop after foliage dies back.
grooming_propagation: Remove spent blooms. Propagate by bulb scales or division.
symptoms: Yellowing = overwater or natural dormancy; spotted leaves = fungal disease.
toxicity_notes: Highly toxic to cats (kidney failure); toxic to kids if ingested. Never mark non_toxic.

description: Often grown in water or pebbles; slender segmented stems. Symbol of good fortune.
fertilizing: Liquid fertilizer very diluted every 2 months; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim stems. Propagate by stem cuttings in water.
symptoms: Yellow stems/leaves = overwater or too much fertilizer; brown = chlorine in water.
toxicity_notes: Toxic to cats and dogs if ingested.

description: Round leaves with silvery stripes like watermelon rind. Compact and pet-safe.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Propagate by leaf or stem cuttings. Trim leggy growth.
symptoms: Dropping leaves = overwater; wrinkled = underwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Single thick heart-shaped leaf (often sold) or vining form with heart leaves.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Propagate by stem cuttings; single-leaf plants rarely grow new leaves.
symptoms: Wrinkled leaf = underwater; yellow = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Trailing succulent with tiny heart-shaped leaves on thin purple stems.
fertilizing: Succulent fertilizer once in spring; none in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim trails. Propagate by stem cuttings or tubers.
symptoms: Shrivelled leaves = underwater; yellow mushy = overwater/rot.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Trailing, slender, spineless cactus stems. Epiphytic; prefers humidity over desert cacti.
fertilizing: Cactus fertilizer once in spring; none in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim stems. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: Wrinkled stems = underwater; soft brown base = overwater/rot.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Small globular cactus with rings of spines and bright spring flowers.
fertilizing: Cactus fertilizer once in spring; none in winter.
grooming_propagation: Propagate by offsets or seed.
symptoms: Soft mushy = overwater/rot; shrivelled = severely underwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids (spines are physical hazard only).

description: Compact citrus with fragrant blooms and edible fruit. Needs bright sun and humidity.
fertilizing: Citrus fertilizer every 4-6 weeks in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Prune to shape. Propagate by grafting or cuttings.
symptoms: Yellow = overwater or nutrient deficiency; leaf drop = cold draft or shock.
toxicity_notes: Oils irritate pets if ingested in quantity; mildly irritating.

description: Carnivorous plant with snap traps. Needs mineral-free water and bright light.
fertilizing: Never fertilize - gets nutrients from insects; stop in winter dormancy.
grooming_propagation: Trim black traps. Propagate by division or leaf pullings.
symptoms: Traps not closing = too little light or dormancy; brown traps = old age or poor water.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Carnivorous vine with pitcher-shaped traps. Needs high humidity and warmth.
fertilizing: Never fertilize; insects only. Pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim brown pitchers. Propagate by stem cuttings.
symptoms: No pitchers = low humidity or light; browning = underwater or cold.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.

description: Low, dense, moss-like ground cover for terrariums. Needs constant moisture.
fertilizing: Balanced liquid very dilute monthly in spring/summer; pause in winter.
grooming_propagation: Trim to keep tidy. Propagate by division or stem cuttings.
symptoms: Browning = dry out (fatal); yellow = overwater.
toxicity_notes: Safe for pets and kids.
